name: Atlas VPN
summary: Zero-day in Atlas VPN Linux client v1.0.3: unauthenticated local API on port 8076 let a malicious website disconnect the VPN and leak the user's IP; publicly disclosed on Reddit in Aug 2023, reported fixed in v1.1 (article date used; disclosure date approximate).

name: ExpressVPN
summary: Vendor's official response (16 Sept 2021) to news about its CIO Daniel Gericke and his earlier work on Project Raven; the vendor says it does not condone Project Raven. Not a breach of ExpressVPN systems. Legal detail of the US case is not in the cited page and is not stated here.

name: Hotspot Shield
summary: Center for Democracy and Technology filed an FTC complaint alleging Hotspot Shield Free VPN (then AnchorFree) engaged in undisclosed data sharing with ad networks and traffic redirection; complaint, not a finding of wrongdoing.

name: IPVanish
summary: Under a DHS summons, IPVanish supplied connection timestamps and source IP for a user despite a no-logs claim; reported by TorrentFreak in 2018 (which names StackPath as the service's new operator).

name: IVPN
summary: Exploited BTCPay Server vulnerability on IVPN's self-hosted Bitcoin payment server let an attacker take Lightning node credentials and move out IVPN operating funds; IVPN says no customer data or customer funds were affected and VPN infrastructure was not involved. Lightning payments were down 7-10 Aug.

name: Mullvad VPN
summary: Swedish police visited Mullvad's Gothenburg office with a search warrant to seize customer data; Mullvad says none existed and police left without taking anything.

name: NordVPN
summary: Vendor disclosure of a breach of a third-party datacenter server (Finland, exposed 2018) and expired TLS key; NordVPN says its network stayed safe.

name: PureVPN
summary: FBI criminal complaint against Ryan Lin (arrest announced Oct 2017) said PureVPN records let investigators determine one customer accessed the service from two originating IPs; reported by The Register as at odds with PureVPN's no-logs claim. Sources report PureVPN later changed its policy (per ProPrivacy, moved to zero-logs in 2018).

name: Windscribe
summary: Two servers seized by Ukrainian authorities; Windscribe says no user data was exposed but an OpenVPN CA key was exposed because servers were not encrypted at rest; led to FreshScribe rebuild.

name: Windscribe
summary: Legal case in Greece against Windscribe's CEO over a Finland server IP was dismissed; no user data was handed over.

name: Windscribe
summary: Dutch authorities physically seized a Windscribe server; per Windscribe it ran RAM-only and held no data.
